message.content: The installer and documentation are in place. I’m correcting the bare-repository hook path handling, then I’ll run the checks available in this environment.
message.reasoning_content:
**Considering repository setup**

I’m thinking about fixing the absolute git directory for my repository and addressing the WEB_ROOT variable. The assignment for the hook environment might be better with a shell-quoted path using printf. It’s tricky with heredoc, though, since I need to interpolate WEB_ROOT correctly and escape script variables, which feels like a lot of work. I’m also concerned about how special characters could lead to potential injection. I want to ensure I'm handling this securely.

function.name: bash
function.arguments:
{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
p='setup-git-web.sh'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('repo=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)\nweb_root=${WEB_ROOT:-/var/www/git-server}', 'repo=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)\nweb_root=$(sed -n \'s/^web_root=//p\' "$repo/hooks/post-receive.conf")')
s=s.replace("chmod 0755 \"$HOOK\"\nchown", "printf 'web_root=%s\\n' \"$WEB_ROOT\" > \"$REPO/hooks/post-receive.conf\"\nchmod 0644 \"$REPO/hooks/post-receive.conf\"\nchown \"$GIT_USER:$(id -gn \"$GIT_USER\")\" \"$REPO/hooks/post-receive.conf\"\nchmod 0755 \"$HOOK\"\nchown")
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
sh -n setup-git-web.sh && sed -n '25,75p' setup-git-web.sh && git --version 2>&1 || true"}
